name: Task-Aligned Tool Recommendation for Large Language Models (PTR: Precision-driven Tool Recommendation)
venue: IJCNLP-AACL 2025 Main (Proceedings of the 14th IJCNLP and 4th AACL); ACL Anthology 2025.ijcnlp-long.110; preprint arXiv:2411.09613 (v1 Nov 2024, v2 Nov 2025)
authors_affiliation: Hang Gao and Yongfeng Zhang, Rutgers University.
code_url: https://github.com/GHupppp/PTR (stated as publicly available in the paper; GitHub API returned 404 at access time, so live accessibility is [uncertain])
task_domain: Tool-use for LLMs (tool selection / tool recommendation prior to query execution).
problem_setting: Offline, single-step, pre-execution recommendation of a precise tool set for a given natural-language query, before any tool is invoked. Single-agent, no runtime/execution feedback. The framework is model-agnostic: an off-the-shelf retriever produces a candidate tool bundle and a backbone LLM (open-mistral-7b, GPT-3.5-turbo, or GPT-4o) drives the functional reasoning. Supervision comes from historical (query, tool-bundle) usage data; no retriever fine-tuning is performed. Evaluated against a known ground-truth toolset per query (exact-solving regime).
what_is_retrieved: tools (external tool/API descriptions), retrieved both as historical tool bundles (sets) and as individual candidate tools; also retrieves similar historical queries to surface their previously-used tools.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed catalog of available tools T plus a fixed set of historical (query, tool-bundle) usage records D. No growing/episodic memory written during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Precision-driven, variable-size recommendation aimed at recovering the COMPLETE minimal-sufficient tool set (exact solving) rather than a fixed top-k ranking. The paper explicitly argues against fixed top-k packaging and defines the objective as T_recommend = T_ground with |T_recommend| = |T_ground| (no over- or under-selection).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, partial-Revise, no-Retain] — Retrieve (tool bundle + similar past queries), Reuse (past tool combinations), Revise (functional coverage mapping prunes/adds tools); no Retain phase (store is frozen, nothing written back). [uncertain] as a strict CBR mapping since the paper does not frame itself as CBR.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it frames the work as 'tool recommendation' analogous to recommender systems / tool retrieval. It does realize CBR-like reuse of historical (query, bundle) cases under another name.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (individual tool description) and tool-bundle (a set of tools co-used in a past query); historical queries are also retrieved as a unit to extract their associated tools.
index_source: Static, offline-induced store: a catalog of all available tools and a corpus of historical (query, tool-bundle) pairs D={(Q_i,B_i)} and the derived set of unique bundles B. Not online/test-time-induced; frozen after construction.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector / lexical index over (a) unique tool bundles, (b) individual tools, and (c) historical queries. No explicit dependency graph or hierarchy is built; inter-tool 'synergies/dependencies' are captured implicitly via co-occurrence in historical bundles rather than an explicit graph topology.
retriever_type: Hybrid set of off-the-shelf retrievers evaluated as the Stage-1 component: sparse (BM25) and dense (Contriever, SBERT all-mpnet-base-v2, TAS-B, SimCSE), plus a Random baseline. Stage-3 multi-view re-ranking uses embedding similarity (sigma) over tools/queries. No LLM-as-retriever or generative tool-as-token retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None / off-the-shelf. Retrievers are used unsupervised/zero-shot (no contrastive fine-tuning, no LM-feedback, no RL). The 'learning signal' is purely the historical tool-bundle co-usage prior leveraged at retrieval/aggregation time, not retriever parameter training.
query_construction: Two-level. Stage-1: raw query Q is matched against historical bundles/queries. Stage-2 (Functional Coverage Mapping): the LLM decomposes Q into a set of discrete key functionalities F={F_1,...,F_m} and, after pruning, emits residual unsolved sub-problems U={U_1,...,U_y}. Stage-3: each unsolved sub-problem U_j is used as a sub-query for multi-view re-ranking. So queries are LLM-decomposed/intent-extracted, not just raw.
query_granularity: Both task-level and sub-problem level (two-level retrieval): bundle retrieval at task level (t=0), then per-unsolved-sub-problem retrieval in the re-ranking stage.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot, multi-stage pipeline executed once per query (retrieve bundle -> map/prune -> re-rank to add). It is not iterative over execution and not uncertainty-triggered; all retrieval happens before execution in a fixed 3-stage schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule (deterministic 3-stage pipeline). Stage-3 re-ranking is triggered only when Stage-2 'Assessment of Toolset Completeness' classifies the bundle as 'Partial Solving' (unsolved sub-problems remain); pruning is triggered on 'Oversolving'. The completeness assessment thus acts as an LLM-judged trigger for add/remove operations.
reranking: Yes. Stage-3 'Multi-view Based Re-ranking' aggregates three candidate tool lists per unsolved sub-problem and re-ranks tools by frequency of occurrence across the three views (a frequency/voting-based, multi-view aggregation rather than a cross-encoder).
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose plus distractor filtering: Stage-2 prunes redundant/unused tools (removing tools that fulfill no required functionality) and identifies gaps; Stage-3 recomposes the set by adding tools for unresolved sub-problems via frequency-based voting across three views. Net effect is a minimal-sufficient (non-redundant, complete) tool set.
tool_document_engineering: Raw tool descriptions/docstrings are used for matching tools to functionalities and for embedding-based similarity; no synthetic-query augmentation, expanded summaries, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings are reported.
index_content_separation: N/A. No explicit lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation is described; tool descriptions are used directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (tools/bundles from ToolLens, MetaTool, RecTools datasets); no live-synchronized tool store, no RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling CRUD auto-sync. Pre-execution recommender, not an execution protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial / implicit. The method argues it captures 'tool dependencies and synergies' by retrieving historical tool bundles (co-used sets) rather than single tools, but there is no explicit dependency graph, bipartite KG, or dependency-aware reranking; dependency is modeled only through co-occurrence in historical bundles.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / tool-set provisioning: the recommended toolset is the output, intended to be supplied to a downstream LLM execution planner as the precise set of tools available before execution. Within PTR, the LLM also uses retrieved tools for reasoning (functional matching, completeness assessment).
planning_integration: Plan-then-retrieve / retrieve-then-refine front-end: a one-shot pre-execution recommender that delivers a lean, capability-complete tool set to downstream execution planners. It is not integrated into MCTS/tree search or per-step interleaved acting; the authors position PTR as a front-end to (distinct from) execution-time tool-use frameworks.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer (one recommendation per query), with internal per-functionality / per-unsolved-sub-problem retrieval inside the single pipeline pass. No per-CoT-step or per-tool-call interleaving during execution.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted adaptation of the retrieved historical bundle: the LLM matches tools to functionalities, classifies completeness (Exact/Over/Partial Solving), prunes redundant tools, and identifies unsolved sub-problems; new tools are then added via frequency-based multi-view re-ranking. No execution-feedback-driven or RL revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form is the tool itself (tool identifier/description) packaged into a recommended toolset; intermediate representations include the LLM-extracted functionality list and unsolved-sub-problem text. No latent/soft tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Mix: reusable co-used tool bundles (procedural/usage-pattern abstraction) at Stage-1 and individual procedural tools (single tool-API units) at Stage-3; functionalities/unsolved-problems are LLM-distilled intermediate abstractions of the query.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Functional Coverage Mapping acts as an LLM relevance evaluator that prunes redundant/unsuitable tools (Oversolving case), and multi-view frequency voting reduces the randomness/noise of selecting tools from the full set (the paper states multi-view ranking 'reduces the randomness associated with selecting tools'). No retriever-aware/distractor-aware SFT training.
memory_type: none (no agent-written episodic/skill memory). Uses a static historical (query, tool-bundle) usage corpus as a read-only prior; this is a fixed database, not a growing memory.
write_back: False. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills back into any memory during deployment; the historical-usage store is frozen.
online_growth: False. The retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is offline-constructed and frozen.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back mechanism exists in the method).
failure_experience_usage: Not used. Only successful historical (query, tool-bundle) usage records inform retrieval; no failed/negative experiences are stored or retrieved. (Stage-2's 'unsolved problems' are within-query gaps, not a failure memory.)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (append-only is not applicable; the store is static and not mutated after construction).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: False. Selection is fixed similarity top-k retrieval plus LLM-prompted reasoning plus frequency-based voting; no learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, no soft Q-learning, no RL retriever).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private pipeline; no memory/experience sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks. (The shared 'historical usage' corpus is a static dataset, not cross-agent runtime sharing.)
benchmarks: ToolLens (from COLT, Qu et al. 2024), MetaTool (Huang et al. 2023), and the newly introduced RecTools dataset. 20% of each dataset used as test data.
benchmark_family: tool (tool-retrieval/recommendation benchmarks): ToolLens and MetaTool are existing tool benchmarks; RecTools is a new multi-tool (1-10 tools per query) tool-recommendation dataset.
baselines: Random (random selection from historical tools), BM25 (sparse), Contriever, SBERT (all-mpnet-base-v2), TAS-B, SimCSE — six standalone retrievers, each also evaluated with +PTR using three backbones (open-mistral-7b, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o). The retrievers alone serve as the fixed-top-k tool-retrieval baselines that PTR is compared against.
key_metrics: TRACC (newly proposed: TRACC = (|A∩B|/|A|) × (1 − ||B|−|A|| / |A∪B|), combining tool-content accuracy/sufficiency and set-size fidelity/minimality), Recall@K, and NDCG@K (with K set to the ground-truth toolset size). Also: average tool-set length difference ||B|−|A|| and per-query API cost.
headline_result: Best configuration SimCSE + PTR + GPT-4o achieves TRACC 0.336 / Recall@K 0.368 / NDCG@K 0.467 on ToolLens, TRACC 0.690 / Recall@K 0.774 / NDCG@K 0.956 on MetaTool, and TRACC 0.591 / Recall@K 0.609 / NDCG@K 0.896 on RecTools (best across all columns). PTR adds large gains over standalone retrievers, e.g. SimCSE+PTR+GPT-4o gives absolute Recall@K improvements of +0.141 (ToolLens), +0.111 (MetaTool), +0.117 (RecTools) over the Random baseline.
ablations: Stage-wise ablation (GPT-4o backbone + SimCSE retriever) removing each of the three stages. w/o Stage-1 (Tool Bundle Acquisition) causes the largest drop (TRACC 0.336->0.235 ToolLens; 0.591->0.439 RecTools), showing historical bundle co-usage is a strong inductive bias. w/o Stage-2 (Functional Coverage Mapping) drops TRACC (e.g. 0.591->0.552 RecTools), key for minimal-sufficient pruning. w/o Stage-3 (Multi-view Re-ranking) drops TRACC (e.g. 0.591->0.566 RecTools), showing multi-view aggregation refines precision. Notably NDCG can stay high while TRACC drops (w/o Stage-1 on RecTools: NDCG 0.916 but TRACC 0.439), validating TRACC.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval/ranking metrics (Recall@K, NDCG@K) are reported alongside the recommendation-precision metric TRACC; the paper explicitly contrasts them to show Recall/NDCG can be high while TRACC (precision/size fidelity) is low. No separate downstream end-to-end task-success metric (e.g. LLM task pass rate) is reported — evaluation is at the tool-set recommendation level only.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-of-recommendation (does the recommended set match the ground-truth set), plus an explicit set-size-quality dimension (average length difference, the TRACC size-penalty term). No downstream execution/trajectory process metrics are measured.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Resource Consumption Analysis (GPT-4o pricing, USD 2.50/M input, 10.00/M output): avg per-query ~USD 0.0055 (ToolLens: 1,638 in + 139 out), ~USD 0.0070 (MetaTool: 2,036 in + 194 out), ~USD 0.0087 (RecTools: 2,657 in + 207 out) — under one cent per query. Motivationally, the method also argues precise toolsets reduce downstream LLM computational overhead vs over-selection. No latency numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Precision-driven / adaptive selection count: PTR determines the tool-set size dynamically per query rather than a fixed k, explicitly targeting |T_recommend| = |T_ground|. For the rank-based metrics, K is set to the ground-truth toolset size. RecTools allows 1-10 tools per query (variable), unlike ToolLens (1-3) and MetaTool (fixed 2).
benchmark_construction_and_size: RecTools: LLM-synthesized — LLMs are prompted to generate specific queries solvable by given tool bundles, then GPT-4o validates 'Exact Solving' (provided tools exactly solve) and 'Partial Solving' (removing one tool yields partial solving), with dedicated validation and deduplication steps; supports 1-10 tools per query (vs ToolLens 1-3, MetaTool fixed 2). Difficulty signal: GPT-4o 'Exact Solving' test pass rate is 61.3% for RecTools vs 55.1% MetaTool and 6.34% ToolLens; for 2- and 3-tool (query,tools) pairs RecTools reaches 76% and 89% success. Exact per-split query/tool counts not given in the paper [uncertain].
builds_on: Tool retrieval and recommendation lineage: COLT/ToolLens (Qu et al. 2024), MetaTool (Huang et al. 2023), Confucius (Gao et al. 2024), classic retrievers BM25/TF-IDF, dense retrievers (Contriever, SBERT, TAS-B, SimCSE, DPR), ToolLLM (Qin et al. 2023); broader LLM-recommendation framing (memory/knowledge/architecture/prompt recommendation).
contrasts_with: Fixed-top-k tool retrieval methods that package a fixed number of top-ranked tools (ToolRerank, COLT, Qu et al. 2024 tool retrieval) and rely on knowing the tool count in advance; ToolkenGPT (tool-as-token). Also explicitly distinguished from execution-time / runtime-feedback tool-use refinement frameworks — Toolformer, Re-Invoke (Chen et al. 2024), DRAFT (Qu et al. 2024), TECTON (Alazraki et al. 2025) — which depend on real tool-execution feedback, whereas PTR is offline pre-execution.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Within retrieval-augmented tool-use, PTR sits in the tool-retrieval/selection sub-lineage but reframes the objective from recall-oriented fixed-top-k retrieval to precision-driven, variable-size tool-set recommendation (minimal sufficient set) as a pre-execution front-end to downstream tool-execution planners.
